title: SDK Empowerment Labs: Onboarding Runbook and Failure-Injection Templates
author: Marco Liang
body:
Overview:
This runbook consolidates the recommended path for SDK onboarding, plus a small lab of failure-injection templates engineers can use to reproduce, triage, and harden integrations with the Redwood API. The goal is to shorten time-to-first-success for client engineers while improving signal for support and product teams when regressions occur.

Intended audience:
- SDK authors and integrators (internal and partner teams)
- Developer experience engineers and on-call support
- Solutions and platform engineers responsible for partner integrations

High-level goals:
- Provide a reproducible local loop for SDK integration testing
- Standardize observability and telemetry for SDKs (request/response, token counts, latency histograms)
- Ship canonical failure-injection templates for common support issues (rate limits, partial responses, stream disconnects, model fallback)
- Document ownership, SLO expectations, and review gates for SDK changes

Quickstart: Local empowerment lab (5–10 minutes)
1) Clone the SDK starter repo and run the local proxy:
   - git clone git@github.com:redwood-inference/dx-sdk-labs.git && cd dx-sdk-labs
   - make local-proxy-start  # spins up the dev proxy with canned responses and telemetry
2) Run the integration smoke test (automated):
   - ./bin/smoke.sh --profile=quickstart
   - Expected: 3 passing checks: auth, generation request, streaming fallback
3) Open the telemetry dashboard (local dev port 9001) to validate spans and token counts.

SDK onboarding checklist (table):
| Step | Required artifact | Owner | Acceptance criteria |
|------|-------------------|-------|---------------------|
| Quickstart demo | README + quickstart example | SDK author | README executes in <10m on mac/linux |
| Auth sample | token+env example | SDK author | Example shows token renewal flow |
| Observability | trace + metric config snippet | DX engineer | Latency histogram and token metric present |
| Canary harness | small script to run 100 reqs | SDK author | No 5xxs in 95% of runs |

Canonical metric names and thresholds:
- sdk.request.latency.p50 / p95 (ms) — target: p95 < 350ms for simple generation requests
- sdk.request.tokens.total — per-request token counter for cost analysis
- sdk.stream.disconnect.count — should be monitored; target: <0.2% over hourly windows
- sdk.backoff.retries.count — track retries after 429/503, target: exponential backoff with jitter and max 5 retries

Observability: telemetry snippet (example YAML for SDK to emit)
---
service: redwood-sdk-client
telemetry:
  traces_exporter: otlp
  metrics_exporter: otlp
  default_sample_rate: 0.25
  labels: ["sdk_name:js", "sdk_version:1.2.0"]
---
Notes:
- Use OTLP/OTEL canonical keys to allow DX dashboards to aggregate across languages.
- Emit token counts as a separate metric with the dimension model_name.

API examples: deterministic test harnesses
- Synchronous generation (cURL):
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/generate 
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" 
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
    -d '{"model":"rw1-small","input":"Summarize: Redwood mission in 20 words","max_tokens":60}'
  Expected JSON: {"id":"req_xxx","status":"ok","choices":[{"text":"...","tokens":42}]}

- Streaming example (node shorthand):
  const r = await client.stream.generate({ model: 'rw1-small', input: 'Hello' })
  r.on('data', (chunk) => { /* append chunk.text */ })
  r.on('end', () => { /* validate final tokens */ })

Failure-injection templates (purpose-built scenarios)
Each template is a small config file in dx-sdk-labs/failures/ and can be activated by the local-proxy with: make inject-failure NAME=<template>. Use these templates in CI canaries and game days.
- template: throttled-429
  scenario: return 429 for the first request of a client session; subsequent requests succeed
  expected-sdk-behavior: respect Retry-After header, backoff + jitter, surface partial telemetry on backoff
- template: partial-stream
  scenario: server sends streaming chunks but closes connection after N chunks (N configurable)
  expected-sdk-behavior: emit stream.disconnect event, attempt reconnect according to stream policy, surface partial output to client UI as fallback
- template: model-fallback-degraded
  scenario: highest-quality model returns 503 for >20% of requests; runtime offers cheaper model variant
  expected-sdk-behavior: automatic fallback per routing policy, telemetry marking fallback reason, degrade QoS metric 

Canonical fixes (top support issues and recommended patches)
1) Symptom: High token cost per request in production
   Fix: Ensure SDKs do not implicitly add repeated system prompts on retries. Audit pre-send hooks and add a de-duplication check that strips repeated prefix tokens. Add metric sdk.request.duplicate_prefix.count.
2) Symptom: Frequent stream disconnects on flaky mobile networks
   Fix: Update client to buffer partial chunks and implement a short reconnect window (2–5s) with session resumption token. Add stream.disconnect tracing and SLOW_NETWORK flag gating.
3) Symptom: Retries amplify error storms (thundering herd)
   Fix: Respect Retry-After, use capped exponential backoff with jitter, and implement global token bucket throttling at client-side when >RPS threshold. Add circuit_breaker.open metric.

Docs site operating procedure (how to publish a new SDK quickstart)
1) Create a branch under docs-sdks/<sdk>/<issue-number>-quickstart
2) Add markdown under /content/sdks/<sdk>/quickstarts; include runnable snippets and a smoke manifest (smoke.yml)
3) Run local docs preview (make docs-preview); validate snippets and embed sandbox links
4) Create PR, include reviewers: DX docs owner + SDK author + accessibility reviewer
5) Merge and trigger staging deploy; validate canonical smoke harness (./bin/smoke.sh --profile=docs)
6) Tag the release and update release_notes/docs-site changelog with the quickstart summary

Release gates and review criteria:
- All code examples must be runnable end-to-end in the dev sandbox within 5 minutes
- Telemetry hooks present and validated in local preview
- Backwards-compatible: do not remove public helper methods without deprecation note and migration guide

Ownership and escalation
- SDK author: primary owner for code and examples; responds to P1 within 1 hour in support rotation
- DX docs lead: owner for copy accuracy and site publish; responds to doc regressions within 8 business hours
- Oncall support: triage production errors; escalate to runtime team for 5xx patterns or capacity-related anomalies

Runbooks for common incidents (short forms)
- Incident: Elevated sdk.stream.disconnect.count > 0.5% for 15 minutes
  1) Confirm: query telemetry for last 30m (dashboard link)
  2) Check proxy/edge logs for TCP errors and client IP distribution
  3) If pattern is region-specific, route traffic to fallback region per routing policy
  4) Engage eng-serving-runtime for kernel-level regressions

- Incident: Canary failing with consistent 429s
  1) Validate client is not sending bursts (inspect client-side rate limiter)
  2) Confirm server-side rate-limit quotas for account (billing/usage console)
  3) If server-side spike, switch canary to dedicated reserved capacity to isolate problem

Testing matrix recommendations
- Local quick smoke: 10 requests, single model, dev proxy
- CI canary: 1000 requests, mixed sequence lengths, record p95 latency and 5xx rate
- Staging soak: 1 hour at 50 RPS using production model catalog

Appendix: useful commands and snippets
- Start local proxy: make local-proxy-start
- Inject a failure template: make inject-failure NAME=throttled-429
- Run smoke: ./bin/smoke.sh --profile=canary
- Export OTLP metrics locally: docker run -p 4317:4317 otel/opentelemetry-collector:latest
